vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: duhui-all-to-pdf
Version: 1.0.0

The skill converts local documents to PDF using a third-party API (Duhui on Alibaba Cloud Market). It exhibits several high-risk behaviors: 'scripts/persist_duhui_appcode.py' modifies shell configuration files (e.g., .bashrc, .zshrc) to persist API keys, and 'scripts/duhui_doc_to_pdf.py' explicitly disables SSL certificate verification using 'ssl._create_unverified_context()', which exposes the agent to Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks. Additionally, the script uploads user documents to a third-party Alibaba OSS bucket (fmtmp.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com) and fetches temporary credentials from a remote endpoint (file.duhuitech.com). While these actions are aligned with the stated purpose of the skill, the combination of shell modification and weakened transport security warrants a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill's code largely matches its claimed purpose (upload a local file to OSS and call Duhui's async convert API), but there are inconsistencies and privacy/credential risks you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the shipped scripts: the tool uploads one local file to an OSS bucket, calls Duhui's v2/convert_async, polls a query endpoint, downloads the PDF, and attempts to delete the temporary OSS object. However the registry metadata declares no required env vars while the runtime explicitly requires DUHUI_DOC_TO_PDF_APPCODE — this mismatch is an incoherence that should be corrected or explained.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs persisting an AppCode into the user's shell startup (via scripts/persist_duhui_appcode.py) and running python scripts that will upload the user's file to a third-party OSS host and call remote APIs. The instructions ask the agent/user to store a secret in shell rc files and to run the included scripts; these are within the conversion purpose but expand scope to persistent local config changes and network I/O of user files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only + bundled Python scripts). The Python scripts use only the standard library; nothing is downloaded or executed during install. This is lower risk from an installation mechanism perspective.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime requires DUHUI_DOC_TO_PDF_APPCODE (AppCode) but the skill metadata declares no required env vars — a discrepancy. The conversion script also fetches temporary OSS credentials from https://file.duhuitech.com/k/tmp_up.json and sets DH_TMP_OSS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET in the process environment to upload the file to fmtmp.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com. That means user files will be uploaded to third-party storage and a remote domain provides upload credentials — behavior that should be explicitly declared and vetted by the user.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). The persist_duhui_appcode.py script will modify the user's shell startup file if the user runs it (inserting export DUHUI_DOC_TO_PDF_APPCODE=...). Writing a secret into shell rc is potentially sensitive (exposes the secret to other processes/users on the host). This modification only happens if the user follows SKILL.md instructions, but the skill encourages doing so.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or running this skill: (1) Understand it will upload your local file to a third‑party OSS bucket (fmtmp.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com) and call remote conversion endpoints; do not use it for sensitive documents unless you trust the vendor. (2) The script expects an AppCode in DUHUI_DOC_TO_PDF_APPCODE — but the registry metadata did not declare this; you should confirm the AppCode is the only required secret. (3) The tool fetches temporary OSS credentials from https://file.duhuitech.com/k/tmp_up.json — verify that domain and the credential provisioning flow are legitimate and acceptable. (4) Persisting the AppCode writes an export line into your shell startup file; prefer setting the AppCode in a single session or an isolated environment instead of permanently adding it to rc files. (5) If you need stronger assurance, run the scripts in an isolated container/VM, inspect network activity during a test run, or ask the publisher to declare required env vars and the credential endpoints in the registry metadata. If you do not trust the vendor or the remote credential host, do not run the scripts on sensitive files.
